newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stock markets attractive -- Standard Life.
newsitem.headline: Indian stock markets attractive -- Standard Life.

text.p: Indian stock markets have become attractive to overseas investors and the outlook is good despite some problems, an investment manager of U.K. insurance firm Standard Life Assurance Company said on Wednesday.

"The market has already rebounded from its (last year's) lows, supported by an improving fundamental environment," Will Hay, investment manager and head of Pacific Basin Equities at Standard Life Assurance told an insurance seminar.
"Corporate earnings should pick up after this year that is just ending (on March 31), providing a solid fundamental background for equity investment from here," Hay said.
The 30-share sensitive index of the Bombay Stock Exchange, India's biggest, almost doubled to 4,029.56 last week from a low of 2,713.12 in the first week of December 1996.
Share prices soared after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram presented India's 1997/98 budget on February 28 with plenty of sops for the stock markets.
Hay said traditional valuation methods such as price earnings ratio now looked much more attracative.

He said dealing in India had become safer after the establishment of the electronic National Stock Exchange. The recent establishment of the National Securities Depository Ltd is expected to ease current problems associated with paper-based settlement system, he said.

"From a foreigner's perspective, there is still a large problem with regard to a tax on portfolio investment in India. This issue should be addressed, making investment in India easier for foreign houses," he said.
"The market is maturing, and I believe an index future could be introduced as early as this year," he said.
These changes will increase liquidity in the Indian stock markets and further encourage investment, he said.
Hay said India had an advantage over many emerging markets in that it offered a great variety of companies for investment.
Exposure to most areas of the economy can be gained through Indian stock market investment unlike in some south-east Asian countries, he added.
But Hay said a major constraint to India's future growth was the fiscal deficit and infrastructure inadequacies.
